title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 94
paragraphs: So the Athenians were at war with the Aeginetans. Meanwhile the Persian was pressing forward with his own design: his servant kept reminding him constantly about the Athenians, and the sons of Pisistratus were near at hand bringing charges against the city without stop, while Darius himself was looking for this very pretext to subdue those parts of Greece that had not given him earth and water. He dismissed Mardonius from command, since his expedition had ended miserably, and appointed other generals to lead the attack against Eretria and Athens: Datis, a Mede by birth, and Artaphernes son of Artaphernes, the king's nephew. He sent them out with orders to reduce Athens and Eretria to slavery and bring the captives before him.
